title: Stateful Agents — Full Workshop with Charles Packer of Letta and MemGPT
talk_summary: Charles Packer (Letta/MemGPT) demonstrates stateful agents where an LLM manages its own memory via tool calls: core memory blocks in-context, plus archival/recall stores outside it, with a server-backed API so agents persist across sessions. He also shows capping the context window, forcing tool-call-only output with reasoning, and multi-agent message passing between independently-running stateful agents.

takeaways.technique: Hard-cap the context window and let a summarizer evict overflow
takeaways.what_they_do: Set an explicit token cap per agent (e.g. 4K-20K); when approaching it, evict messages to recall memory and run a configurable summarizer so the payload never exceeds the cap.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you'll never go over 4K. Um and if you go over 4K by accident ... we run we evict a certain amount of messages into the recall memory
takeaways.numbers: caps cited: 4K, 8K, 10K, 20K; warns 200K payloads mean 'minutes on a response'

takeaways.technique: Make every LLM turn a tool call (including send_message)
takeaways.what_they_do: Force the model to always emit a tool call plus a reasoning field; even replying to the user is a send_message tool, so the agent can run in the background without speaking and loops are explicit.
takeaways.evidence_quote: even when the agent wants to just say hello to the user, it has to call a tool called send message

takeaways.what_they_do: Invert ReAct: the agent must explicitly set a continue flag to get another loop iteration, rather than looping until it declares completion.
takeaways.evidence_quote: in letter leta we actually do the inverse where the agent has to say I want to keep going ... much less likely the agent will derail

takeaways.what_they_do: Memory blocks are DB rows with IDs that multiple agents can link to; a write by one agent is immediately visible to all sharers, avoiding duplication.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can have these blocks like linked together so multiple agents can have the same block ... when one writes the block it like immediately gets broadcasted

takeaways.technique: Split memory tools into a separate 'subconscious' agent
takeaways.what_they_do: Move memory-management tools off the main agent onto a shadow agent sharing the same blocks, because too many tools degrade tool selection.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you go above like 12 15 tools you start to get degradation

takeaways.what_they_do: Agents run as separate server-backed services and talk via send-message tools (async fire-and-forget, sync wait-for-reply, or tag-broadcast to a group); removing a tool detaches an agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: multi-agent just means message passing and you can just have agents like wire to each other over APIs
